reasoning.Student A:
This is a school choice/matching mechanism with priorities, which strongly resembles the Deferred Acceptance (Gale-Shapley) algorithm. A key property of DA is that truthful reporting of preferences is a dominant strategy for participants — misreporting cannot improve your outcome and could only hurt you. 

Looking at my priorities: I have top priority (1) at w and y, and lower priority (2) at x and z. Since most other applicants rank y > x > w > z, competition for w and z (where most others rank them low) will likely be lower, which works in my favor since z is my top choice and w is my second choice. My high priority at w and y also protects me somewhat at those schools.

Given DA's strategy-proofness, the optimal strategy is simply to submit my true preference ordering: z > w > y > x. This ensures I get matched to the best possible school given my priorities and the reported preferences of others, without risking a worse outcome from strategic misreporting.
